headline_marked: [[Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir sworn in as 23rd President]] of Bangladesh; cabinet reshuffle follows
headline: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir sworn in as 23rd President of Bangladesh; cabinet reshuffle follows
summary: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir took his oath as the 23rd President at Bangabhaban, administered by the Acting Speaker. This was followed by four new ministers and two state ministers being sworn in.
details: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has been sworn in as the 23rd President of Bangladesh. The ceremony took place at Bangabhaban, where Acting Speaker Barrister Kayser Kamal administered the oath of office.
The newly appointed President received floral greetings from the outgoing acting President. Dignitaries and high-ranking officials were present to witness the significant event.
Following the presidential oath, four new ministers and two state ministers also took their oaths. This marks a significant cabinet reshuffle under the new presidency.
The Cabinet Division subsequently issued a gazette notification, officially assigning portfolios to the newly sworn-in ministers and state ministers. This clarifies their roles within the government.
Leaders from various nations, including the Presidents of India, Nepal, and Pakistan, have extended their congratulations to President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on his assumption of office.
caption:
Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has officially taken office as Bangladesh's 23rd President, marking a new chapter for the nation.

Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has been sworn in as the 23rd President of Bangladesh. The ceremony took place at Bangabhaban, where Acting Speaker Barrister Kayser Kamal administered the oath of office.

The newly appointed President received floral greetings from the outgoing acting President. Dignitaries and high-ranking officials were present to witness the significant event.

Following the presidential oath, four new ministers and two state ministers also took their oaths. This marks a significant cabinet reshuffle under the new presidency.

The Cabinet Division subsequently issued a gazette notification, officially assigning portfolios to the newly sworn-in ministers and state ministers. This clarifies their roles within the government.

Leaders from various nations, including the Presidents of India, Nepal, and Pakistan, have extended their congratulations to President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on his assumption of office.

headline_marked: [[2 arrested for online Hilsa fraud]] in Chandpur, police recover Tk 60,000
headline: 2 arrested for online Hilsa fraud in Chandpur, police recover Tk 60,000
summary: Two members of an organized gang have been arrested in Chandpur for defrauding people by advertising Hilsa fish and other products on social media. Police recovered Tk 60,000, mobile phones, and SIM cards.
details: Chandpur District Detective Police (DB) arrested two members of an organized gang for online fraud, who advertised Hilsa fish and other products on social media to deceive buyers. Police recovered five mobile phones, SIM cards, and Tk 60,000 from their possession.

Additional Superintendent of Police (Crime & Ops) Md. Lutfor Rahman confirmed the arrests on Friday, August 21. The arrested individuals were identified as Md. Habibur Rahman alias Sajid (41) and Md. Rakibul Hasan Nayan alias Rabbi (36).

The arrests were made on Thursday night following a general diary filed at Chandpur Sadar Model Police Station and complaints from various victims. Operations were conducted in Noagram, Purulia Union, Kalia Upazila, Narail, and Chandpur Madhyapara areas.

The gang used various Facebook pages to post attractive advertisements for Hilsa fish and other goods. They would then collect money from customers via mobile banking and bank accounts, but fail to deliver the promised products.

Preliminary investigations revealed that the arrested individuals had been involved in online fraud for a long time, collaborating with their associates. They have been accused under the Cyber Security Act, 2026, and relevant sections of the Penal Code. They were subsequently sent to court.

Chandpur Superintendent of Police Md. Mizanur Rahman urged the public to properly verify unknown individuals or Facebook pages before engaging in online transactions. This advisory aims to prevent further instances of online fraud.
